summary: Autopilot provisioning stalls: duplicate hardware hash caused by OEM NIC image cloning
description: Issue summary: Multiple newly-received corporate Windows laptops stall during Autopilot provisioning at 'Waiting for device registration' / 'Applying device identity' stage. Impact: New hires and desk-swaps cannot complete setup; blocking access to corporate apps. First observed on 2026-03-09 in US West onboarding hub. Root cause hypothesis: several vendor-preloaded vendor images include a NIC firmware/driver layer that clones MAC/UDID values, producing identical hardware hashes in Autopilot and causing registration to be rejected as duplicates.
impact: ~22 devices blocked over 48 hours; delays in onboarding for 8 new hires; ticket volume spike to IT helpdesk. Affects autopilot self-provisioning flow for devices using vendor preimage builds.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Take vendor-preloaded device with OEM image and connect to provisioning network.
2) Start Autopilot OOBE flow and sign in with corp account.
3) Provisioning stalls at 'Applying device identity' with no progress for >20 minutes.
4) Check Autopilot portal: device appears with 'duplicate hardware hash' error or does not register.
5) Reimage same hardware from bare-metal clean image -> provisioning completes successfully.
logs: Autopilot logs (device): EventID 60007 - 'Device registration failed: Duplicate hardware hash detected'
SCCM/OSD log (vendor image machine): kernel reports identical NIC GUID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 in two separate units
Network trace snip: DHCP lease requests show same client identifier across affected devices
investigation_notes: Confirmed repro by imaging two different serial-numbered units with vendor image -> both present same hardware hash in Autopilot portal.
Checked vendor-supplied provisioning script (provided in hardware box) and found a stage that writes a persistent NIC GUID file; value was a static template in their build pipeline.
Workaround validated: clean bare-metal reimage (corporate image) clears the duplicated identifier and Autopilot registration succeeds.
Cross-check with AssetDB: imported serials were correct, but gateway reject happens at Autopilot level due to identical HWID, so asset database mismatches are downstream symptom rather than cause.
SRE note: no network-wide DHCP conflict — duplicate client IDs originate from device image content, not infrastructure.
Risk: if vendor continues shipping this preimage, large batches may be blocked at provisioning and create onboarding backlog.
Related tickets: flagged similar symptom in INT-50321 (serial-normalization mismatch) but root cause differs.

workaround: Manual bare-metal reimage using corporate imaging station clears duplicate hardware identifiers and allows Autopilot registration. For affected hires, IT will perform reimage and expedite provisioning. Temporary policy: reject vendor-preloaded devices at intake and send to imaging queue until vendor patch is confirmed.
resolution: Partial: confirmed workaround (reimage) and vendor committed to fix factory imaging. Long-term fix: add automatic preflight validation in intake pipeline to detect cloned NIC/GUID artifacts, and block outbound vendor batches until vendor confirms patched pipeline. Follow-up action assigned to Vendor Relationship Manager to enforce remediation SLA.

2) IT to add NIC/GUID preflight check to intake automation and block affected batches (PR merged -> roll out by 2026-03-15).
3) Update onboarding runbook with temporary intake policy and reimage escalation flow.
